Contribute: 439 studies need metadata

The pipeline recovers per-sample metadata from archive attributes, supplementary tables and papers — but for the studies below it could not. Each row says what is missing, why (the blocker) and what would unlock it. If you know the study (you are an author, a lab member, or you have read the paper) you can often supply the missing table or key in minutes.

How to contribute

Five kinds of contribution

TypeWhat to send
per_sample_tablePer-sample table (CSV/TSV/XLSX keyed by run or BioSample accession)
id_keyID key (sample name ↔ BioSample/run accession)
paper_pointerPaper pointer (PMID/DOI of the study's own paper)
age_scheduleAge schedule (timepoint label → age in days)
verdict_evidenceVerdict evidence (is this study infant gut shotgun metagenomics?)

A table keyed by run accession (SRR/ERR/DRR) or BioSample (SAMN/SAMEA/SAMD) joins directly. Tables keyed by the paper's own sample names (e.g. T1_S23) need an ID key as well — the archive holds no such names. Ages as numbers with a unit; controlled vocabularies are in Fields.

Licence and privacy

By contributing you confirm that the uploaded table may be redistributed under CC-BY-4.0, or you ask that only derived values be published (the file is then kept privately for audit). Upload research metadata only: no participant names, no e-mail addresses, no free-text clinical notes. Your GitHub login is the provenance record; it is stored hashed in the package.

What happens next

  1. Contribute opens a prefilled GitHub Issue (label contribution); drag-and-drop your CSV/TSV/XLSX (≤ 50 MB) into the note field. A GitHub account is needed.
  2. Deterministic ingest (daily): the pipeline downloads the attachment, records its sha256 and checks whether an identifier column joins to the study's own run accessions, sample keys, sample titles or library names. It comments on the Issue with a verdict — accepted_for_review, unjoinable (with the ID form it saw and what key is missing), duplicate_of_existing or rejected (type/size). Nothing you upload is executed.
  3. Curator review: accepted tables go through the same extraction contract as journal supplements (route R2, every value with evidence, conflicts to the conflict queue — never a silent overwrite).
  4. Next release: applied values carry release_added and the study page shows the attribution ("per-sample table contributed by <login>, <date>").

Claim a task to avoid duplicate effort: comment "working on it" on the study's Issue (open one with the Contribute button if none exists yet). Open contribution Issues: github.com › OlmLab/infant-gut-catalog › issues · label:contribution.

Worklist (439 studies, ranked by priority)

Priority = Σmissing fields weight × (1 − coverage) × log10(catalog-scope samples + 1); weights age 3 · delivery 2 · feeding 2 · preterm 1.5 · antibiotics 1 · probiotic 0.5. Coverage = fraction of the study's catalog-scope samples with a value; a field counts as missing below 50%. Recoverability tier per field (R1 archive attribute … R4 abstract, R0 none) is the pipeline's pre-extraction prediction. Source: contribute_worklist.csv · contribute_worklist_fields.csv · JSON. Release R2026.7.

How to cite: Microbiome Repo, release R2026.7 (data package 1.8.0), OlmLab, 2026-09-28.
Caveats: every value carries a route (R1 archive attribute, R2 supplementary table, R3 paper text, R4 abstract/description), a scope and a confidence tier (not a calibrated probability); R3/R4 values are group-level statements applied to samples — see Fields and Methods › Limitations. Built with an LLM-assisted pipeline; treat individual values as evidence-linked claims, not ground truth. Found an error? Every study, cohort and sample has a Flag an issue button that opens a prefilled GitHub issue. Know a study's missing metadata? See Contribute.
